```{r setup, include = FALSE}

library(nlmixr2lib)
library(PKNCA)
library(rxode2)
library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)
```

# Model and source

```{r model}
mod <- readModelDb("Duong_2025_clobetasolPropionate")
ui <- rxode2::rxode(mod)
```

* Citation: `r ui$reference`
* Article: <https://doi.org/10.1002/bcp.70102>
* Full text and supplement:
  <https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pmc/articles/PMC12569561/>

# What this model is, and what it is not

Duong 2025 builds a Simcyp (version 22) physiologically based pharmacokinetic
(PBPK) model of the potent topical corticosteroid clobetasol propionate (CP).
A full-PBPK distribution layer, built and checked on intravenous and oral
data (Study A), is coupled to Simcyp's multi-phase multi-layer MechDermA
dermal absorption model. That model was calibrated on topical cream and
ointment studies in healthy men, then extended with a skin-barrier-impairment
model for lesional and non-lesional skin in atopic dermatitis (AD). The
paper's headline results are simulations of local (stratum corneum) and
systemic exposure by formulation, skin condition and treated body-surface
area (Table 9, Figure 6).

Simcyp's whole-body mass-balance equations and its MechDermA skin model are
proprietary and do not appear in the paper. The distribution layer uses
Rodgers and Rowland tissue:plasma partition coefficients with an optimised
`Kp` scalar of 0.22. Table 6 prints that scalar and the resulting
steady-state volume, but no tissue `Kp`, organ volume or blood flow, so the
multi-tissue structure cannot be rebuilt. The paper does report, completely,
what the **intravenous** disposition needs:

* the in vivo systemic clearance input, 27 L/h (Table 6, "CLIV from
  Study A");
* its renal component, 0.12 L/h (Table 6);
* the final model's steady-state volume of distribution, 2.34 L/kg
  (Table 6). The `Kp` scalar was optimised so that this matches the observed
  Study A volume of 164 L (Methods, "Intravenous administration");
* and, in Table 7, the PBPK model's own predicted half-life and AUC after the
  2 mg intravenous dose. These are the answer key for any reduction.

That is enough for a one-compartment intravenous reduction with no fitted
parameter. Below, it reproduces the platform's predicted AUC to within 8% and
its half-life to within 20%.

## Why the topical arms are not reproduced

MechDermA is a one-dimensional diffusion model. Drug partitions out of an
evaporating two-phase vehicle into a "brick-and-mortar" stratum corneum,
whose many lipid and corneocyte sub-layers each have their own geometry,
hydration and partition coefficients. It then diffuses through the viable
epidermis, dermis, a hair-follicle shunt, subcutis and muscle into a local
blood supply (Supplementary Figure S2; the equations are in a cited Simcyp
reference, not in this paper). The paper prints the drug-specific inputs
(Tables 3, 4 and 6) and, for the abdomen site only, the number of
stratum-corneum layers and the viable-epidermis and dermis thicknesses
(Table 5 footnotes). It does not print:

* the transport equations themselves;
* the per-site skin geometry for the back, thigh, lower leg and arms, which
  carry most of the applied dose in every whole-body study (Tables S4-S6);
* dermal blood flow, hair-follicle density and geometry, or subcutis and
  muscle thickness.

These are Simcyp system-database values, and no amount of reading the paper
recovers them. The published outputs (Table 7 and Table 9) are simulated
summaries, not a parameterisation. Fitting a simpler absorption model to them
would make a new model of the maintainers' own, not a reproduction of the
paper's. The atopic-dermatitis scenarios are a further layer on top of
MechDermA (Table 5: 80% and 26% thinner skin for lesional and non-lesional
skin, plus hydration, pH and corneocyte-size changes), so they are out of
scope for the same reason. The paper's systemic-to-local findings are
summarised in the model's `population$notes`.

## Why the oral arm is not reproduced

The oral arm (Supplementary Table S1) adds a first-order absorption rate
`ka = 0.86 1/h` and a fraction absorbed `fa = 0.5`. In Simcyp the
bioavailability is `fa * Fg * Fh`. `Fg` and `Fh` are platform outputs that
depend on gut and hepatic blood flows, which the paper does not print. The
paper's own predictions show that they matter:

```{r oral-falsifier}
dose_po   <- 2                       # mg, Study A (Table 1)
cl_iv     <- 27                      # L/h, Table 6
vc_red    <- 2.34 * 70               # L, Table 6 at 70 kg
ka_po     <- 0.86                    # 1/h, Table S1
fa_po     <- 0.5                     # Table S1
auc_iv_pb <- 80.1                    # ng*h/mL, Table 7 predicted AUC0-inf, 2 mg IV
auc_po_pb <- 33.0                    # ng*h/mL, Table S2 predicted AUC0-inf, 2 mg oral
tmax_po_pb <- 1.1                    # h, Table S2 predicted median Tmax

f_implied <- auc_po_pb / auc_iv_pb   # same dose, linear PK: AUC ratio = F
auc_fa    <- fa_po * dose_po / cl_iv * 1000
k_red     <- cl_iv / vc_red
tmax_red  <- log(ka_po / k_red) / (ka_po - k_red)

oral_chk <- tibble::tibble(
  Quantity = c("Bioavailability implied by the PBPK predictions (AUC_po / AUC_iv)",
               "Printed fraction absorbed fa",
               "Unprinted Fg * Fh needed to close the gap",
               "AUCinf from fa * dose / CL_iv (ng*h/mL)",
               "PBPK-predicted oral AUC0-inf (ng*h/mL)",
               "One-compartment Tmax with ka = 0.86 1/h (h)",
               "PBPK-predicted oral Tmax (h)"),
  Value = signif(c(f_implied, fa_po, f_implied / fa_po, auc_fa, auc_po_pb,
                   tmax_red, tmax_po_pb), 4)
)
knitr::kable(oral_chk, caption = "Why the oral arm is not reduced.")

stopifnot(
  abs(f_implied - 0.412) < 0.001,
  auc_fa / auc_po_pb > 1.10,         # fa alone overshoots by ~12%
  tmax_red / tmax_po_pb > 2          # mono-exponential Tmax is ~2x too late
)
```

Two independent gaps rule the oral arm out:

* **Bioavailability.** Taking `fa = 0.5` as the whole bioavailability
  over-predicts the platform's oral AUC by 12%, because the platform's `F` is
  about 0.41. The missing `Fg * Fh` of about 0.82 is a platform output that
  the paper does not print. Adopting 0.41 would mean deriving `F` from the
  answer key, which reproduces the answer by construction and validates
  nothing.
* **Shape.** With a single 164 L volume, `ka = 0.86 1/h` puts Tmax at 2.4 h
  against the 1.1 h that the platform predicts and Study A observed. The
  early peak comes from a small initial distribution volume (about 18 L in the
  original Study A two-compartment analysis) that a mono-exponential
  reduction cannot carry. For an intravenous dose this only affects the first
  hour or so, but after an oral dose it moves the peak.

# Population

```{r population}
p <- ui$population
pop_tab <- tibble::tibble(
  Field = c("Species", "Studies", "Subjects", "Age", "% female", "Disease",
            "Doses"),
  Value = c(p$species, p$n_studies, p$n_subjects, p$age_range,
            p$sex_female_pct, p$disease_state, p$dose_range)
)
knitr::kable(pop_tab, caption = "Intravenous Study A (Duong 2025 Table 1).")
```

The intravenous layer comes from Study A (Table 1): an unpublished 1983
Glaxo bioavailability report in which six healthy men received 2 mg CP
intravenously and orally. Plasma was sampled to 30 h and urine collected to
30 h. The paper reports no age or body weight for these subjects.

The paper as a whole used 12 clinical studies. Five were topical studies in
healthy men (Studies B to D and Harding 1985; whole-body applications of
12.5-30 g of 0.05% cream or ointment). One measured stratum-corneum
concentrations by tape stripping (Au 2010, 30 men and women). Three were in
adults with AD (Hehir 1983, Sparidans 2010 and van Velsen 2012; Table 2).
Simulations used the Simcyp Healthy Volunteer population, matched to each
study's sex split and age range, with at least 100 virtual subjects per study
(Tables S4-S6).

# Source trace

Every value in the `ini()` block, with its source location.

```{r source-trace}
trace_tab <- tibble::tribble(
  ~Parameter,    ~Value,      ~Source,
  "lvc",         "163.8 L",   "Table 6 'Vss (L/kg)' 2.34; 2.34 L/kg * 70 kg (matches the 164 L Study A Vss in Methods)",
  "lcl_renal",   "0.12 L/h",  "Table 6 'CLR (L/h)' 0.12; abstract and Table 7 (observed CLR 0.12 L/h)",
  "lcl_nonren",  "26.88 L/h", "Table 6 'CLIV (L/h)' 27, minus the 0.12 L/h renal arm",
  "propSd",      "0 (fixed)", "No residual-error model is reported anywhere in the source"
)
knitr::kable(trace_tab, caption = "Source trace for every fixed parameter.")
```

The model equations are the standard one-compartment intravenous system
(`d/dt(central) = -kel * central`, `kel = cl / vc`, `cl = cl_renal + cl_nonren`,
`Cc = 1000 * central / vc`) with no nonstandard terms. The `1000` converts
mg/L to the ng/mL used in Figure 2 and Table 7.

```{r derivation-gate}
theta <- ui$theta
stopifnot(
  isTRUE(all.equal(exp(theta[["lvc"]]), 2.34 * 70, tolerance = 1e-8)),
  isTRUE(all.equal(exp(theta[["lcl_renal"]]), 0.12, tolerance = 1e-8)),
  isTRUE(all.equal(exp(theta[["lcl_renal"]]) + exp(theta[["lcl_nonren"]]),
                   27, tolerance = 1e-8)),
  # The volume at 70 kg reproduces the 164 L Study A Vss the Kp scalar was
  # optimised to.
  abs(exp(theta[["lvc"]]) / 164 - 1) < 0.005
)
cat("All model parameters reproduce the Duong 2025 arithmetic.\n")
```

# Virtual cohort

The model has no random effects, so it is deterministic and one subject fully
describes the regimen. The regimen is Study A's single 2 mg intravenous dose,
given as a bolus (Figure 2 shows the simulated profile starting at its peak
at time zero). The observation grid runs to 30 h, the end of the sampling
window and of the Table 7 AUC0-30h.

Observations are placed on the `central` ODE state, and `Cc` is returned as an
algebraic observable on those rows.

```{r cohort}
arm_lab <- "Study A: 2 mg IV bolus"
obs_grid <- seq(0, 30, by = 0.05)

events <- dplyr::bind_rows(
  tibble::tibble(id = 1L, time = 0, amt = 2, evid = 1L, cmt = "central",
                 arm = arm_lab),
  tibble::tibble(id = 1L, time = obs_grid, amt = NA_real_, evid = 0L,
                 cmt = "central", arm = arm_lab)
) |>
  dplyr::arrange(id, time, dplyr::desc(evid))

stopifnot(!anyDuplicated(events[, c("id", "time", "evid")]),
          sum(events$evid == 1L) == 1L)
```

# Simulation

```{r simulate}
# Tight step tolerances: the closed-form gates below compare against exact
# identities, so the integrator error must sit well under their bounds.
sim <- rxode2::rxSolve(mod, events = events, keep = "arm",
                       rtol = 1e-10, atol = 1e-12) |>
  as.data.frame()

# rxSolve omits the id column for a single-subject solve; restore it for
# PKNCA grouping.
if (!"id" %in% names(sim)) sim$id <- 1L

stopifnot(all(is.finite(sim$Cc)), all(sim$Cc > 0))
```

# Replicate published figures

Figure 2 of Duong 2025 shows the simulated mean CP plasma profile after the
2 mg intravenous dose, its 5th-95th percentile band and the six observed
individual profiles, on a log scale. The observed data were not digitised
here. The plot shows the reduction's profile together with the platform's
predicted and the observed terminal half-lives from Table 7, drawn as
reference slopes through the reduction's 30 h value.

```{r figure-2, fig.width = 7, fig.height = 4.5}
c30 <- sim$Cc[sim$time == 30]
slopes <- tidyr::crossing(
  tibble::tibble(source = c("PBPK-predicted t1/2 5.2 h",
                            "Observed t1/2 3.9 h"),
                 thalf = c(5.2, 3.9)),
  time = seq(10, 30, by = 0.5)
) |>
  dplyr::mutate(Cc = c30 * exp(log(2) / thalf * (30 - time)))

ggplot(sim, aes(time, Cc)) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 0.8) +
  geom_line(data = slopes, aes(colour = source), linetype = "dashed") +
  scale_y_log10() +
  labs(x = "Time (h)", y = "Plasma clobetasol propionate (ng/mL)",
       colour = NULL,
       caption = paste("Replicates Figure 2 of Duong 2025 (reduction's",
                       "profile only).\nDashed: Table 7 terminal",
                       "half-lives as reference slopes.")) +
  theme_bw() +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom")
```

The reduction starts at `dose / Vss` (12.2 ng/mL). In Figure 2 the platform's
mean profile falls from about 100 ng/mL to roughly 15 ng/mL within the first
half hour. That is the rapid distribution phase into a small initial volume,
which a single-volume model omits. Between about 1 h and 20 h the reduction
stays close to the platform's mean. Read approximately off Figure 2, the
platform's mean is about 1.8 ng/mL at 10 h (reduction 2.4) and about
0.45 ng/mL at 20 h (reduction 0.45). After that, the reduction's shorter
half-life carries it below the platform's mean: about 0.09 against
0.14 ng/mL at 30 h, at the low edge of the observed values. Its terminal
half-life (4.2 h) lies between the platform's 5.2 h and the observed 3.9 h.

# PKNCA validation

```{r pknca}
conc <- sim |>
  dplyr::filter(!is.na(Cc)) |>
  dplyr::select(id, time, Cc, arm)

dose_df <- events |>
  dplyr::filter(evid == 1L) |>
  dplyr::select(id, time, amt, arm)

stopifnot(nrow(conc) > 0, nrow(dose_df) == 1L, any(conc$time == 0))

conc_obj <- PKNCA::PKNCAconc(conc, Cc ~ time | arm + id,
                             concu = "ng/mL", timeu = "h")
dose_obj <- PKNCA::PKNCAdose(dose_df, amt ~ time | arm + id,
                             doseu = "mg", route = "intravascular")

intervals <- data.frame(
  start = c(0, 0),
  end = c(30, Inf),
  auclast = c(TRUE, FALSE),
  aucinf.obs = c(FALSE, TRUE),
  half.life = c(FALSE, TRUE)
)

nca <- PKNCA::pk.nca(PKNCA::PKNCAdata(conc_obj, dose_obj,
                                      intervals = intervals))

nca_df <- as.data.frame(nca) |>
  dplyr::filter(PPTESTCD %in% c("auclast", "aucinf.obs", "half.life"))

knitr::kable(
  nca_df |>
    dplyr::mutate(PPORRES = signif(PPORRES, 4)) |>
    dplyr::select(arm, start, end, PPTESTCD, PPORRES, PPORRESU),
  caption = "PKNCA results for the simulated 2 mg intravenous dose."
)
```

## Closed-form gates

For a one-compartment model after an intravenous bolus, `AUCinf = dose / CL`
and the terminal half-life is `log(2) * vc / cl`, both exactly. These
identities check the NCA setup as much as the model.

```{r closed-form-gate}
get_nca <- function(p) {
  v <- nca_df$PPORRES[nca_df$PPTESTCD == p]
  if (length(v) != 1L) stop("no unique NCA row for ", p)
  v
}

vc_mod <- exp(theta[["lvc"]])
cl_mod <- exp(theta[["lcl_renal"]]) + exp(theta[["lcl_nonren"]])

gate <- tibble::tibble(
  Quantity = c("AUC0-inf (ng*h/mL)", "AUC0-30h (ng*h/mL)", "t1/2 (h)"),
  NCA = c(get_nca("aucinf.obs"), get_nca("auclast"), get_nca("half.life")),
  Closed_form = c(2 / cl_mod * 1000,
                  2 / cl_mod * 1000 * (1 - exp(-cl_mod / vc_mod * 30)),
                  log(2) * vc_mod / cl_mod)
) |>
  dplyr::mutate(pct = 100 * (NCA / Closed_form - 1))

knitr::kable(
  gate |>
    dplyr::mutate(dplyr::across(where(is.numeric), \(x) signif(x, 5))) |>
    dplyr::rename("Closed form" = Closed_form, "% diff" = pct),
  caption = "NCA output vs. the closed-form one-compartment identities."
)

# All three are exact for this model; what remains is trapezoidal error on
# the 0.05 h grid and ODE integration error. The bound sits well above the
# achieved agreement but far below any parameter-level mistake (a wrong
# volume or clearance moves these by tens of percent).
stopifnot(max(abs(gate$pct)) < 0.5)
```

# Comparison against the published NCA

## Against the paper's own PBPK predictions

This comparison decides whether the reduction is faithful to the platform
model. Table 7 reports the PBPK model's predicted half-life and AUC for
Study A. Its clearance row (26.2 L/h predicted, 27.6 L/h observed) is not
tabulated separately: after an intravenous dose, clearance is dose / AUC0-inf,
which the AUC0-inf row already tests. Nothing was tuned to reach these values.

```{r nca-compare-pred}
nca_cmp <- nca_df |>
  dplyr::select(arm, PPTESTCD, PPORRES)

published_pred <- tibble::tribble(
  ~arm,     ~auclast, ~aucinf.obs, ~half.life,
  arm_lab,  78.2,     80.1,        5.2
)

cmp_pred <- nlmixr2lib::ncaComparisonTable(
  simulated = nca_cmp,
  reference = published_pred,
  by        = "arm",
  units     = c(auclast = "ng*h/mL", aucinf.obs = "ng*h/mL",
                half.life = "h"),
  tolerance_pct = 20
)

knitr::kable(
  cmp_pred,
  caption = paste("Reduction vs. the Simcyp predictions in Duong 2025",
                  "Table 7 (Study A, 2 mg IV; AUC0-30h in the auclast row).",
                  "* differs by >20%."),
  align = c("l", "l", "r", "r", "r")
)
```

```{r nca-gate-pred}
# `% diff` is formatted as text (a trailing "*" marks rows over tolerance),
# so strip the formatting before testing. The solve is deterministic, so
# these bounds do not have to absorb any cohort sampling noise.
pct_pred <- suppressWarnings(
  as.numeric(gsub("[^0-9.eE+-]", "", as.character(cmp_pred[["% diff"]])))
)
stopifnot(sum(is.finite(pct_pred)) == 3L,
          max(abs(pct_pred), na.rm = TRUE) < 20)
cat(sprintf(paste("All %d comparisons against the PBPK predictions agree",
                  "within 20%%; largest discrepancy %.1f%%.\n"),
            sum(is.finite(pct_pred)), max(abs(pct_pred), na.rm = TRUE)))
```

How to read the table:

* **AUC runs low by 6-8%.** The platform's simulated clearance runs slightly
  below its own 27 L/h input: the predicted AUC0-inf implies
  2 mg / 80.1 ng*h/mL = 25.0 L/h. The reduction uses the 27 L/h that Table 6
  gives as the model input and does not adopt the platform's simulated
  output. Because the dose is flat (no body-weight dependence), the ratio
  25.0 / 27 = 0.925 accounts for the whole AUC0-inf gap. The platform's
  reported mean clearance of 26.2 L/h is a mean of individual clearances,
  which sits above dose divided by mean AUC.
* **The half-life is 19% short of the platform's.** This is the cost of the
  mono-exponential reduction. The platform's terminal phase reflects slow
  return from peripheral tissues, while the reduction's single volume gives
  `log(2) * 163.8 / 27 = 4.2 h`. The observed Study A half-life (3.9 h)
  sits closer to the reduction than to the platform.

## Against the observed data

Table 7 also reports the observed Study A values (mean, with standard error).
They are shown for completeness; they test the platform model as much as the
reduction.

```{r nca-compare-obs}
published_obs <- tibble::tribble(
  ~arm,     ~auclast, ~aucinf.obs, ~half.life,
  arm_lab,  73.3,     74.8,        3.9
)

cmp_obs <- nlmixr2lib::ncaComparisonTable(
  simulated = nca_cmp,
  reference = published_obs,
  by        = "arm",
  units     = c(auclast = "ng*h/mL", aucinf.obs = "ng*h/mL",
                half.life = "h"),
  tolerance_pct = 20
)

knitr::kable(
  cmp_obs,
  caption = paste("Reduction vs. observed Study A values in Duong 2025",
                  "Table 7. * differs by >20%."),
  align = c("l", "l", "r", "r", "r")
)

pct_obs <- suppressWarnings(
  as.numeric(gsub("[^0-9.eE+-]", "", as.character(cmp_obs[["% diff"]])))
)
stopifnot(sum(is.finite(pct_obs)) == 3L,
          max(abs(pct_obs), na.rm = TRUE) < 10)
```

The paper's acceptance criterion is a predicted/observed ratio between 0.5 and
2.0. The reduction is within 10% of every observed Study A value.

# Assumptions and deviations

1. **Body weight of 70 kg is assumed.** Table 6 states the volume in L/kg,
   and no body weight for Study A appears in the paper or its supplement. The
   70 kg reference is the standing rounded standard, and the paper
   corroborates it: the `Kp` scalar was optimised to match the observed Study A
   volume of 164 L, and 164 / 2.34 = 70.1 kg. `WT` is recorded in
   `covariatesDataExcluded` rather than carried as a live covariate. The
   clearance is an absolute 27 L/h, so scaling volume alone would make the
   model internally inconsistent.
2. **Only the intravenous arm is reproduced.** The topical cream and
   ointment arms, the occlusion scenario, the atopic-dermatitis
   skin-barrier-impairment model, the stratum-corneum concentrations and the
   area-by-skin-condition simulations (Tables 7-9, Figures 3-6) all run
   through Simcyp's MechDermA model, whose equations and per-site skin
   physiology the paper does not print. The oral arm is not reduced for the
   two reasons shown above (unprinted `Fg * Fh` and a Tmax that a single
   volume cannot reproduce).
3. **The reduction is mono-exponential.** The source is a full-PBPK model
   and only a lumped `Vss` is reported, so no distribution phase can be
   reconstructed. The original Study A analysis reported an initial volume of
   about 18 L, but no inter-compartmental clearance, and it is a
   two-compartment fit of the data rather than the PBPK model. The cost is a
   missing early spike (first half hour) and a terminal half-life 19% shorter
   than the platform's.
4. **The clearance is the input, not the platform's output.** Table 6 gives
   27 L/h as the in vivo clearance input. The Methods describe the Study A
   mean of 27.6 L/h as the *initial* estimate, and the Discussion repeats
   27.6 L/h, but the final parameter table and the abstract both give 27 L/h,
   which is used here. The platform's simulated clearance (26.2 L/h mean,
   25.0 L/h from dose/AUC) is not adopted, since that would be tuning toward
   the answer key.
5. **Two misprints in the source were resolved from the paper itself.**
   * The Methods ("Intravenous administration") give the Study A renal
     clearance as "2 L/h". Table 6, Table 7 (observed 0.12, predicted
     0.11 L/h) and the abstract all give 0.12 L/h, which is used.
   * Table 7 lists the Study A intravenous dose as "0.02" g. Table 1 states
     2 mg, and the observed AUC0-inf (74.8 ng*h/mL) times the observed
     clearance (27.6 L/h) gives 2.06 mg, so 2 mg is used.
6. **The intravenous dose is given as a bolus.** Table 1 does not state an
   infusion duration, and Figure 2's simulated profile starts at its peak at
   time zero.
7. **No inter-individual variability and no residual error.** Duong 2025 is
   a PBPK simulation study, not a population-PK fit. Its 5th-95th percentile
   bands are the spread of a Simcyp virtual population driven by unpublished
   population files, not estimated variance components. Rather than invent
   variances, the model has no etas and `propSd` is fixed at zero, so it is a
   deterministic typical-value simulator.
8. **Elimination is split only into renal and non-renal arms.** Table 6
   prints CP's elimination as an in vivo clearance with a renal component,
   and no enzyme-level split. The renal arm is carried as `lcl_renal`
   because the paper prints it as a clearance; it does not change the plasma
   profile.
9. **No errata were found.** A EuropePMC search on 2026-11-10 found no
   correction notice for doi:10.1002/bcp.70102.
